--- title: "S0-03 notebook — R" subtitle: "Build a data-check battery and grade it" execute: freeze: auto --- Eleven realistic defects have been injected into a copy of `CASE-SM`. Build the checks, then grade yourself against the manifest. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(dplyr) LLOQ <- 1 raw <- read.csv("../../cases/case-sm/data/ozanib_pk_messy.csv", colClasses = c(ID = "character")) cat(sprintf("%d rows, %d subjects\n", nrow(raw), n_distinct(raw$ID))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 2643 rows, 60 subjects ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} head(raw, 4) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|ID | TIME| NTIME| DAY| AMT| DV| EVID| MDV| CMT| BLQ| DOSE| WT| AGE| SEX| CRCL| ALT| DDI| IPRED_TRUE| |:--|----:|-----:|---:|---:|--------:|----:|---:|---:|---:|----:|---:|---:|---:|----:|---:|---:|----------:| |1 | 0.0| 0.0| 1| 25| NA| 1| 1| 1| 0| 25| 118| 54| 0| 106| 22| 0| NA| |1 | 0.0| 0.0| 1| NA| NA| 0| 1| 2| 1| 25| 118| 54| 0| 106| 22| 0| 0.0000| |1 | 0.5| 0.5| 1| NA| 100.5463| 0| 0| 2| 0| 25| 118| 54| 0| 106| 22| 0| 120.7391| |1 | 1.0| 1.0| 1| NA| 176.9772| 0| 0| 2| 0| 25| 118| 54| 0| 106| 22| 0| 165.5341|
::: ::: Note `colClasses = c(ID = "character")`. Reading identifiers as text is a habit worth forming: `007` becomes `7` otherwise, and then a merge silently drops a subject. ## The battery Each check appends to a findings list rather than stopping, so one run reports everything at once. In production, `stop()` at the end if the list is non-empty — a build that continues past a failed check is not a check. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} findings <- list() flag <- function(code, msg, ids = character()) { findings[[length(findings) + 1]] <<- list(code = code, message = msg, ids = sort(unique(as.character(ids)))) } ``` ::: ### C01 · Identifier format ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bad <- unique(raw$ID)[unique(raw$ID) != as.character(as.integer(unique(raw$ID)))] if (length(bad)) flag("ID_FORMAT", sprintf("%d ID(s) not canonical", length(bad)), bad) ``` ::: ### C02 · Duplicate event keys ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} key <- raw |> count(ID, TIME, EVID, CMT) |> filter(n > 1) if (nrow(key)) flag("DUP_RECORDS", sprintf("%d duplicated event key(s)", nrow(key)), key$ID) ``` ::: ### C03 · Negative time ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} d <- raw |> filter(TIME < 0) if (nrow(d)) flag("NEGATIVE_TIME", sprintf("%d record(s) with TIME < 0", nrow(d)), d$ID) ``` ::: ### C04 · Dose must sort before an observation at the same time ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bad <- raw |> group_by(ID, TIME) |> filter(n() > 1, first(EVID) == 0, any(EVID == 1)) |> ungroup() |> pull(ID) if (length(bad)) flag("DOSE_ORDER", "observation sorts before the dose at the same TIME", bad) ``` ::: ### C05 · Regular dosing intervals ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bad <- raw |> filter(EVID == 1) |> group_by(ID) |> summarise(irregular = { g <- diff(sort(TIME)) length(g) > 0 && any(abs(g - median(g)) > 1e-6) }, .groups = "drop") |> filter(irregular) |> pull(ID) if (length(bad)) flag("MISSING_DOSE", "irregular gap in the dosing sequence", bad) ``` ::: ### C06 · Zero used to mean missing ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} d <- raw |> filter(EVID == 0, !is.na(DV), DV == 0) if (nrow(d)) flag("ZERO_MEANS_MISSING", sprintf("%d observation(s) with DV exactly 0", nrow(d)), d$ID) ``` ::: ### C07 · BLQ consistency ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} d <- raw |> filter(EVID == 0, !is.na(DV), DV < LLOQ, BLQ == 0) if (nrow(d)) flag("BLQ_IMPUTED", sprintf("%d value(s) below LLOQ not flagged", nrow(d)), d$ID) ``` ::: ### C08 · Unit switch A within-subject comparison is far more sensitive than a population range check, because it does not have to see through between-subject variability. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bad <- raw |> filter(EVID == 0, !is.na(DV), TIME > 0) |> group_by(ID) |> summarise(n_early = sum(TIME < 240), n_late = sum(TIME >= 240), med_early = median(DV[TIME < 240]), med_late = median(DV[TIME >= 240]), .groups = "drop") |> filter(n_early > 2, n_late > 0, med_late < med_early / 100) |> pull(ID) if (length(bad)) flag("UNIT_SWITCH", "late concentrations >100x lower than early ones", bad) ``` ::: ### C09 · Covariate plausibility ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} d <- raw |> filter(WT < 35 | WT > 250) if (nrow(d)) flag("IMPOSSIBLE_COVARIATE", "body weight outside 35-250 kg", d$ID) ``` ::: ### C10 · Baseline covariates constant within subject ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cols <- c("AGE", "SEX", "WT", "DOSE") nuniq <- sapply(cols, \(c) max(tapply(raw[[c]], raw$ID, \(x) length(unique(x))))) bad_cols <- names(nuniq)[nuniq > 1] if (length(bad_cols)) { ids <- unlist(lapply(bad_cols, \(c) { n <- tapply(raw[[c]], raw$ID, \(x) length(unique(x))); names(n)[n > 1] })) flag("TIME_VARYING_BASELINE", sprintf("baseline covariate(s) vary within subject: %s", paste(bad_cols, collapse = ", ")), ids) } ``` ::: ### C11 · Dose magnitude ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} d <- raw |> filter(EVID == 1, AMT < 1 | AMT > 1000) if (nrow(d)) flag("DOSE_UNIT", "AMT outside a plausible 1-1000 mg range", d$ID) ``` ::: ## The report ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} for (f in findings) { ids <- paste(head(f$ids, 6), collapse = ",") if (length(f$ids) > 6) ids <- paste0(ids, "...") cat(sprintf("%-22s %-55s -> ID %s\n", f$code, f$message, ids)) } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ID_FORMAT 1 ID(s) not canonical -> ID 050 DUP_RECORDS 4 duplicated event key(s) -> ID 3 NEGATIVE_TIME 1 record(s) with TIME < 0 -> ID 27 DOSE_ORDER observation sorts before the dose at the same TIME -> ID 36 MISSING_DOSE irregular gap in the dosing sequence -> ID 8 ZERO_MEANS_MISSING 1 observation(s) with DV exactly 0 -> ID 22 BLQ_IMPUTED 43 value(s) below LLOQ not flagged -> ID 11,12,13,14,31 UNIT_SWITCH late concentrations >100x lower than early ones -> ID 11,12,13,14 IMPOSSIBLE_COVARIATE body weight outside 35-250 kg -> ID 44 TIME_VARYING_BASELINE baseline covariate(s) vary within subject: AGE -> ID 5 DOSE_UNIT AMT outside a plausible 1-1000 mg range -> ID 19 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} cat(sprintf("\n%d check(s) failed\n", length(findings))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 11 check(s) failed ``` ::: ::: ## Grade yourself ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} manifest <- read.csv("../../cases/case-sm/data/ozanib_pk_messy_manifest.csv") found <- sapply(findings, \(f) f$code) injected <- manifest$code cat(sprintf("injected : %d\n", length(injected))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` injected : 11 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} cat(sprintf("detected : %d\n", length(intersect(found, injected)))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` detected : 11 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} cat(sprintf("missed : %s\n", paste(setdiff(injected, found), collapse = ", "))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` missed : ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} cat(sprintf("spurious : %s\n", paste(setdiff(found, injected), collapse = ", "))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` spurious : ``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-important} Look at which subjects trip **C07**. Subjects 11–14 appear there as well as in **C08**, because dividing their concentrations by a thousand pushed them below the LLOQ. One injected defect, two independent alarms — the argument for running the whole battery rather than stopping at the first failure. ::: ## Now fix them ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data.frame( code = c("ID_FORMAT", "DUP_RECORDS", "NEGATIVE_TIME", "DOSE_ORDER", "MISSING_DOSE", "ZERO_MEANS_MISSING", "BLQ_IMPUTED", "UNIT_SWITCH", "IMPOSSIBLE_COVARIATE", "TIME_VARYING_BASELINE", "DOSE_UNIT"), response = c( "normalise in the assembly script, re-run every join", "de-duplicate on the event key AFTER confirming they are true duplicates", "decide the reference time; a screening sample may belong to a prior period", "re-sort ID, TIME, then EVID descending", "recover from source EX; if unrecoverable, exclude the interval and log it", "set to NA with MDV = 1; never carry a 0 into a log-scale model", "restore the flag from the raw assay export; do not un-impute by arithmetic", "confirm against the laboratory report, then convert once at the boundary", "query the site; do not silently correct a decimal point", "take the baseline visit value; check the join key", "confirm against source EX, then convert once") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|code |response | |:---------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------| |ID_FORMAT |normalise in the assembly script, re-run every join | |DUP_RECORDS |de-duplicate on the event key AFTER confirming they are true duplicates | |NEGATIVE_TIME |decide the reference time; a screening sample may belong to a prior period | |DOSE_ORDER |re-sort ID, TIME, then EVID descending | |MISSING_DOSE |recover from source EX; if unrecoverable, exclude the interval and log it | |ZERO_MEANS_MISSING |set to NA with MDV = 1; never carry a 0 into a log-scale model | |BLQ_IMPUTED |restore the flag from the raw assay export; do not un-impute by arithmetic | |UNIT_SWITCH |confirm against the laboratory report, then convert once at the boundary | |IMPOSSIBLE_COVARIATE |query the site; do not silently correct a decimal point | |TIME_VARYING_BASELINE |take the baseline visit value; check the join key | |DOSE_UNIT |confirm against source EX, then convert once |
::: ::: Three of these — the missing dose, the impossible weight, the unit switch — cannot be resolved inside the analysis at all. **A check you "fix" by guessing has been converted from a defect you know about into a defect you do not.** ## What to try next 1. Add a check that every subject has at least one observation after their last dose. 2. Generalise C08: flag any subject whose residual variability against a naive pooled fit is an order of magnitude worse than the population median. 3. Wrap the battery in a function that `stop()`s on any finding and run it as a pre-commit hook. That is the version that actually protects you.
